summary: Recommend acceptance as a bounded manuscript input, with one minor source-note repair and no blocking scientific findings. The review is saved at reviews/AMMT_WRITING/attempt-2.json and was verified to parse with the required schema keys. The actual Results and Discussion file exists and contains approximately 1,502 words before its author-facing notes. Its geometry values, uncertainty-scale ratios, B-to-C contrasts, passage times, factorial effects and numerical qualifications agree with the supplied evidence and checked retained originals. The revised speed sentence correctly restricts attribution to the fixed-power B-to-C comparison. The draft leads with model discrepancy, preserves nonblind data roles, separates experimental and model observation operators, and confines closure interpretation to the fixed-B model. Acceptance applies to this section input; it does not establish physical validation, real-property identification, novelty or journal readiness.

findings.reason: Minor factual locator defect in author-facing note N4: it names a dossier section called 'High-temperature continuation factorial and mechanism', which does not exist in the supplied dossier. The relevant heading is 'Fixed-B 2×2 continuation contrast' under 'Condition trends and mechanism evidence'. Affected material is the N4 evidence locator for the fixed-B closure competition and rear-boundary interpretation. The numerical claims themselves are supported by the valid JSON pointers and original constitutive-factorial-results.json. Repair the heading in N4 before integrating the notes; no new computation is needed. No claim identifiers were supplied, so the affected claims are identified by their text and note label rather than invented IDs.
evidence_paths: inputs/evidence-dossier.md: Condition trends and mechanism evidence / Fixed-B 2×2 continuation contrast

limitations: The request exposed the producer's sentence-repair summary and supporting numerical interpretation before review. The dossier itself also contains interpretation. I inspected the assigned inputs before reading the manuscript, but this was not a blind review. I did not consult attempt-1.json. Same-model review does not confer statistical independence.

Beyond the assigned dossier and verified data, I accessed the retained original experimental-comparison.csv, constitutive-factorial-results.json, six production result.json files, calibrated-neighborhood summary.json, constant-property analytic geometry report, Lane section 2.3 lines 675–747, and original numerical modelVerification.tex lines 320–440. These support the consequential comparisons and operator distinction. No solver was imported or rerun, and raw temperature arrays and full executed source bindings were not independently re-audited in this review.

Raw AMMT thermography series and microscope boundary picks remain unavailable in the supplied package, preventing full measurement-operator replay and covariance reconstruction. NIST width/depth means and Lane expanded uncertainties are separately sourced populations. The draft discloses this and uses their ratios descriptively; these comparisons do not support combined-uncertainty coverage claims.

Branch-specific multidirectional convergence, experimentally identified high-temperature constitutive properties, independent predictive conditions and cross-speed factorials are absent. The draft limits its claims accordingly. These gaps do not block the existing discrepancy and major-tail-response prose; they would affect stronger physical, causal or precision claims.

No contemporary literature search or journal-instruction audit was performed. The retained original numerical source corroborates the opposite isotropic geometry bias and fitted directional-conductivity precedent, but the coordinator still needs verified bibliographic entries and a defensible contribution assessment before submission. No invented references were found in the section.
